about: The priest asks God to look favorably upon the offering and accept it, as He accepted the gifts of the just Abel, the sacrifice of Abraham, and what Melchisedech offered to Him. Genesis calls Melchisedech a priest of God most high, and it is the Canon that calls him a high priest.

seg.nr: The priest spreads his hands and goes on.

seg.tr: Deign to look upon them with a gracious and serene countenance and to regard them as accepted, as You deigned to accept the gifts of Your righteous servant Abel and the sacrifice of our Patriarch Abraham:

fn.w002: A relative pronoun referring to the offerings named in the preceding prayer.
fn.w003: Together with “seréno” (w005), it modifies “vultu” (w006): with a gracious and serene countenance.
fn.w011: In the phrase “accépta habére”: “to regard as accepted”.
fn.w015: The perfect participle of the deponent verb “dignor”. With “es” (w016), it forms the perfect tense.
fn.w021: An indeclinable name: only “púeri” (w018), which it stands in apposition to, shows the genitive.
fn.w026: The one of the three names Latin declines: Ábraham, Ábrahæ.

nt.w020: The adjective may belong to púeri, Thy just servant, or to the name Abel itself. Both readings stand in the translation tradition. This edition attaches it to the name.

seg.tr: and what Your high priest Melchisedech offered to You: a holy sacrifice, a spotless Victim.

fn.w028: A relative pronoun without an expressed antecedent: “that which he offered”. Two appositions follow it.
fn.w031: It modifies “sacérdos” (w032). In Genesis 14:18 Melchisedech is called “sacérdos Dei altíssimi” — “priest of God most high”.
fn.w034: An indeclinable name, nominative in apposition to “sacérdos” (w032). Melchisedech is the subject of “óbtulit” (w030). Genesis 14:18 says that he brought out bread and wine.
fn.w036: The first apposition to “quod” (w028): “a holy sacrifice”.
fn.w038: The second apposition to “quod” (w028). Feminine “hóstiam” and neuter “quod” share the accusative case.
